note: The per-family closure surface for Q14 (`zero-input`, catalogue category `zeroInput`) at GOAL_SPEC.md 9.1. It publishes the outputs 1 to 10 status list for this one family, with the exact evidence behind each applicable output and an explicit justification for anything not applicable. Every count in this artifact was measured from a runner report produced by demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-proof-family-q14.mjs in this tree: one batched `aiken check -e` invocation under the pinned fork compiler for the on-chain selectors, and one Vitest run per cited suite. Nothing is counted from test source, from prose, or from a sibling artifact's numbers. LOCAL_PASS is the only passing status this artifact may record; the live half of a family's closure is owned exclusively by the Q57 sweep and QG3 and is never recorded in a family-local artifact. Outputs 5 to 8 are bound family-locally in the SHARED four-family artifact docs/exec-plans/evidence/canonical-v1-proof-family-q1x-v1.json, whose own gate demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-proof-family-q1x.mjs is the executable authority for those cells and runs in the same battery; this artifact records the delegation explicitly, re-reads the shared artifact's Q14 cells, and re-checks that the concrete Q14 surfaces those cells describe exist and are wired, rather than re-running the shared suites a second time. Output 10 is OPEN: the two parent-owned matrices are measured below and neither records this family's local status yet. Four structural differences from the Q10, Q11 and Q12 twins are measured rather than inherited. First, this family owns TWO blocks of the shared emulator suite rather than one — an end-to-end lifecycle and a dedicated negative — so each block's markers are scoped to its own `it` block, the two counts are published separately, and the negative's adversarial assertion is measured rather than assumed. Second, this family DOES open one of the nine section-2.5 committed fields (field 0, spend inputs) through the section-8.8 door, so output 3 binds that field positionally against both spec tables and against the on-chain and off-chain index constants, instead of measuring an absence the way the Q12 twin does. Third, the reason the section-549/612 spend-input cardinality axis does not reach this family is therefore narrower than Q12's and is measured from source: the finalizing step pins the opened field's AUTHENTICATED ITEM COUNT to zero, so any proof that finalizes carries the one-byte empty preimage and the axis's admissible 296-input stress cannot reach this family's success path. Fourth, the redeemer's nested carriage enum is tracked on both sides of the boundary, so its constructor order is bound POSITIONALLY rather than as a set of names.

compiler.rationale: The identity is measured from the spawned binary and required to match EXACTLY, not by prefix: a second fork build of the same 1.1.23 base reports a different `+<rev>` suffix and would supply this family's on-chain result under a compiler .github/workflows/aiken-ci.yml does not pin. The stock v1.1.22 that used to compile the blueprint carries a live unsound-codegen defect and is retired from every role, so no on-chain count in this artifact may come from it.

output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.rule: A Midgard L2 transaction must spend at least one input. Phase A rejects a transaction whose `spendInputs` collection is empty (`if (tx.spendInputs.length === 0)`), before any input can be resolved; the on-chain correction path proves the same fact about a transaction the block header already committed to, by opening the transaction's section-2.5 spend-inputs field and reading its authenticated item count as zero.

localEnforcement.note: One site, and the rejection call is a SINGLE line, so the opener line and the token line are the same. The gate therefore requires the opener at or above the token line and requires that line to BEGIN the rejection call, rather than demanding the multi-line shape the Q10/Q11/Q12 siblings happen to have — a gate tuned to a sibling's formatting would fail here on a correctly enforced rule.

measuredNonEnforcementMentions.role: A cross-check comparison, not a rejection: it reads a rejection code that phase A already produced. Published so that "the count above is an enforcement count" rests on a measured exclusion rather than only on the openers of the sites that were counted.

catalogueBinding.note: The deployed identifier is the positional index of the append-only order encoded over 4 bytes, so it is re-derived from the order constant rather than read from a constant. Inserting a category rather than appending one silently re-numbers every family after it, and this family sits at index 5 with five earlier insertion points ahead of it.

authoritySections: ### 8.8 Carriage wire types (consumers outside the validation machine)

fieldIndexConstants.note: The positional identity, bound in all three places it exists: section 2.5 index 0, the on-chain constant, and the off-chain table. This is not trivia for this family. Section 4 removed field-index domain separation, so the empty preimage of every one of the nine fields hashes to the same value; the INDEX is the only thing that makes this an opening of field 0 rather than of some other empty field, which is why the whole off-chain table is checked positionally and not just the one entry.

authenticatedCountAssertion.note: This is the family's verdict, and it is an authenticated COUNT read rather than a hash comparison. The validator's own comment states why: section 4 removed field-index domain separation, so all nine empty fields share one commitment and a hash equality against a pinned empty-field constant would prove only that SOME field is empty. Positional identity lives inside the section-8.8 door, and reading the count out of the opened view is how this family gets it. The module's third selector exists to defend exactly that distinction.

builderDoorBinding.note: The off-chain half of the same door. The builder must name the positional index table rather than a bare integer, and that requirement is derived from the table's own entry name rather than hard-coded.

builderAnchorBinding.note: The first step re-derives the transaction id from the compact bytes the block's `transactions_root` committed and writes it into thread state as `bad_tx_id`; `requireNativeTxMatchesCompactCbor` is what makes that id the committed transaction's rather than the prover's. That anchor is the only provenance `BodyAnchor` accepts in the terminal step, so a step-01 that stopped re-deriving it would leave the door opened against an unanchored id.

output4OnchainSelectors.scopeNote: Every selector's scope is DERIVED, not declared: the gate resolves whether the selector's own body reaches the module's `main.spend` handler, directly or through a module-local helper that itself does, over the comment-stripped source. All eight reach it, so this family has no module-helper unit cases and its positive count and its step-scoped positive count coincide. The distinction is kept in the schema because output 4's per-step requirement is stated on the step-scoped positives: a module-local unit case added later must not be able to satisfy that requirement with the real proof-step positives deleted.

selectors.claim: Drives the deployed step-01 handler over a native V1 block fixture: the challenged transaction's compact bytes are shown included under the header-authenticated counted `transactions_root`, and the thread advances carrying the re-derived section-2.5 anchor.

The same passage over the issue-545 published-chunk carriage: the membership proof's levels live in published chunk UTxOs and only their order reaches the redeemer, and the step accepts it under the same authenticated root.
A published-chunk carriage whose chunks were assembled under a root the header never committed is refused, so the cheaper carriage cannot be used to smuggle in an unauthenticated root.
A chunk reference the redeemer's index list does not name cannot be counted toward the proof, so the prover cannot rely on chunks that happen to be present in the transaction.

The step's valid-block negative: a raw transactions MPF root the challenged header's counted `transactions_root` does not authenticate is refused, so no block can be convicted on a prover-supplied root.
Drives the deployed terminal handler to finalization: field 0 of the anchored transaction is opened through the section-8.8 door and its authenticated item count is zero, so the fraud proof mints.
The family's valid-block negative: a challenge against a transaction that really does spend inputs cannot finalize, so an honest block cannot be convicted by this family.

The selector that defends the flat scheme's sharpest edge for this family: an empty section-5.1 preimage presented for a transaction that spends inputs is refused. Because section 4 removed field-index domain separation, all nine empty fields share one commitment, so a design that compared a forwarded commitment against a pinned empty-field constant would accept this. Reading the count out of the door does not.

delegatedOutputs.rationale: Those four cells are bound family-locally in the shared four-family artifact, and its gate is the executable authority for them: it spawns five Vitest suites, three of them emulator suites driving the complete correction path at forced branch level 22 and at the admissible 296-input Cardano spend shape. Re-running them here would double the battery's cost and measure nothing the shared gate does not already measure. So this artifact records the delegation, re-reads the shared artifact's Q14 cells, and re-checks in this tree that the concrete Q14 surfaces those cells describe exist and are wired.

assertedCells.carriageDispositionNote: This family rides ONE of the shared artifact's two carriage remediations. The issue-545 membership-proof depth remediation has measured it, and membership in that list is hard-required. The issue-612 tier-routed spend-input remediation has not, and rather than hard-code that absence, it is DERIVED from the axis's own scope list and required to agree in both directions: demanding this family in the tier-routed list would produce a row that can never go green, while dropping the axis silently would hide the obligation if the axis ever grew to cover it. Output 9 is asserted here as well as measured locally, so the two artifacts cannot disagree about this family's emulator cell.
assertedCells.note: The delegation contract may not be relaxed from the artifact side: LOCAL_PASS is the only status that carries a cell, and a shared artifact with any open cell left in it is not a settled authority for four of this family's rows.

spendInputAxisSourceSweep.reason: The Q12 twin could back the axis's absence with "no step of this family opens a committed field at all". This family DOES open one, so the absence rests on something narrower, and it is measured rather than asserted: the finalizing step pins the opened field's authenticated item count to zero (`expect field_item_count(spend_inputs_view) == 0`), so any proof that FINALIZES carries the one-byte empty section-5.1 preimage and cannot grow with spend-input cardinality. The axis's 296-input admissible-shape stress therefore cannot reach this family's success path, which is why the axis's own scope list names only Q10 and Q11. The sweep publishes every field-opening and `spend_inputs*` token in all four family-owned Aiken modules, so a second opening or a relaxed count pin lands here rather than passing unseen, and it requires the door to live in exactly the finalizing validator: an opening in the first step would put a preimage on the carriage of a step the depth axis does reach.

output8.note: One submit verb per deployed step; every non-terminal step returns `nextThreadOutRef` so the next step is addressable from the previous submission alone, and the terminal step is required NOT to return one and to return the permanent `fraudProofUnit` instead. demo/midgard-sdk/src/fraud-proof/zero-input.ts carries a stale docstring around `EMPTY_SPEND_INPUTS_HASH` describing it as the value "which is what `fraud_proofs/zero_input/step_02` compares against". The deployed step compares nothing of the kind: it opens field 0 and asserts the authenticated item count is zero. The constant itself remains useful off-chain for detection, so this is a comment fix rather than a code fix, but it is the kind of comment that would talk a future reader back into an unsound design.

Worth recording where a future family will look for it: because section 4 removed field-index domain separation, the empty preimage of every one of the nine committed fields hashes to the same value, so for a family whose verdict is "this field is empty" the field commitment alone carries no positional identity at all. Positional identity lives inside the section-8.8 door, which is handed the field index and authenticates the count. Any new family that decides a rule from an empty field must read the count through the door rather than compare a commitment, and must bind the index constant on both sides the way output 3 does here.
